canada.title: Minimum wage hasn't kept pace with the cost of living across Canada, new reports show
canada.summary: Of the 59 cities and regions in reports for every province reviewed by CBC News, none had a provincial minimum wage equal to the calculated living wage — the amount a full-time worker needs to meet their basic needs, manage unexpected expenses and participate meaningfully in their community.

canada.title: Ontario's Bill 140 raises concerns over landfill approvals, groundwater protection in Caledon, Ont.
canada.summary: Ontario's proposed Bill 140 would remove a municipal support requirement for certain large landfills, prompting concerns about groundwater and the time available for Caledon's incoming council to respond.

canada.title: New mayors in Haldimand, Norfolk, Brant, Brantford take office this week
canada.summary: The city of Brantford and the counties of Brant, Haldimand and Norfolk will this week swear in new mayors elected in Ontario's municipal election last month.

canada.title: Montreal's deteriorating Dieppe Park to get $35M makeover — but not any time soon
canada.summary: Montreal is planning a $35-million makeover for Dieppe Park, including replacing its crumbling riverfront retaining wall. But surfers, fishermen and visitors will have to wait until 2029 for work to begin, and even that tentative date depends on further planning and environmental approvals.

canada.title: Quebec assumes parents help pay for post-secondary schooling. Students say many can't
canada.summary: Thousands of post-secondary and university students held strikes across Quebec this week to denounce “austerity measures and growing precariousness” among students in the face of the rising cost of living and the provincewide housing crisis. Among other things, the coalition is calling for a reform of Quebec's student financial aid program.

No passengers or crew killed or critically hurt after tanker collides with river cruise ship on Mississippi, officials say

A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard Friday, the mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on…

More than 100 passengers and crew were rescued after a tanker struck a river cruise on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, prompting a massive rescue operation that sent 32 people to the hospital. NBC News’ George Solis reports.
The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
According to the Port of New Orleans, all 197 passengers and crew members have been accounted for. "No critical injuries have been reported," it said in a post on social media.
